title: Malta Year 8 Math Chapter 8 — Algebra Word Problems
question: Four stories with two unknown prices. Write the two equations yourself, then solve them.
intro:
- Each story has two things with unknown prices.
- Read the story and write two equations yourself, one for each person or family.
- Solve them to find both prices.
- In stories 3 and 4, part (c) asks how many ways there are to spend a budget exactly.
- Type money as a number only, for example 2.5 for 2.50 euros.

questions.title: Pens and notebooks · (a) one pen
questions.prompt:
At a stationery shop in Sliema, all pens cost the same and all notebooks cost the same.

Maria buys 4 pens and 3 notebooks and pays 15 euros.

Daniel buys 2 pens and 5 notebooks and pays 18 euros.

(a) How much does one pen cost?

Type the euros as a number only.
questions.solution:
Call the price of one pen \(x\) euros and the price of one notebook \(y\) euros.

Write one equation for each:

\[4x + 3y = 15 \;\;\text{(1)}\]

\[2x + 5y = 18 \;\;\text{(2)}\]

Make the number of pens the same: multiply (1) by 2 and (2) by 4.

\[8x + 6y = 30\]

\[8x + 20y = 72\]

Take one away from the other, so the pens disappear:

\[14y = 42\]

\[\begin{aligned} y &= 42 \div 14 \\ &= 3 \end{aligned}\]

Put \(y = 3\) back into (1):

\[4x + 3 \times 3 = 15\]

\[\begin{aligned} 4x &= 15 - 9 \\ &= 6 \end{aligned}\]

\[\begin{aligned} x &= 6 \div 4 \\ &= 1.50 \end{aligned}\]

Check with (2): 2 × 1.50 + 5 × 3 = 18.

It matches.

\[\boxed{1.50}\text{ euros}\]

questions.title: Coffee and pastizzi · (a) one coffee
questions.prompt:
At a kiosk in Valletta, every coffee costs the same and every pastizz costs the same.

Ryan orders 3 coffees and 4 pastizzi and pays 8.40 euros.

Leah orders 2 coffees and 7 pastizzi and pays 8.20 euros.

(a) How much does one coffee cost?

Type the euros as a number only.
questions.solution:
Call the price of one coffee \(x\) euros and the price of one pastizz \(y\) euros.

Write one equation for each:

\[3x + 4y = 8.40 \;\;\text{(1)}\]

\[2x + 7y = 8.20 \;\;\text{(2)}\]

Make the number of coffees the same: multiply (1) by 2 and (2) by 3.

\[6x + 8y = 16.80\]

\[6x + 21y = 24.60\]

Take one away from the other, so the coffees disappear:

\[13y = 7.80\]

\[\begin{aligned} y &= 7.80 \div 13 \\ &= 0.60 \end{aligned}\]

Put \(y = 0.60\) back into (1):

\[3x + 4 \times 0.60 = 8.40\]

\[\begin{aligned} 3x &= 8.40 - 2.40 \\ &= 6 \end{aligned}\]

\[\begin{aligned} x &= 6 \div 3 \\ &= 2 \end{aligned}\]

Check with (2): 2 × 2 + 7 × 0.60 = 8.20.

It matches.

\[\boxed{2}\text{ euros}\]

questions.group: Q3 · Two books and a gift budget
questions.title: Two books · (a) one copy of book A
questions.prompt:
A bookshop sells two books for school: book A and book B.

Nina gets 60 euros from her parents.

She buys 3 copies of book A and 2 copies of book B, and gets 8 euros back.

Karl gets 95 euros from his parents.

He buys 5 copies of book A and 3 copies of book B, and gets 13 euros back.

(a) How much does one copy of book A cost?

Type the euros as a number only.
questions.solution:
Call the price of one copy of book A \(x\) euros and the price of one copy of book B \(y\) euros.

First find the money spent.

Nina spends 60 − 8 = 52 euros.

Karl spends 95 − 13 = 82 euros.

Write one equation for each:

\[3x + 2y = 52 \;\;\text{(1)}\]

\[5x + 3y = 82 \;\;\text{(2)}\]

Make the number of copies of book A the same: multiply (1) by 5 and (2) by 3.

\[15x + 10y = 260\]

\[15x + 9y = 246\]

Take one away from the other, so the copies of book A disappear:

\[y = 14\]

Put \(y = 14\) back into (1):

\[3x + 2 \times 14 = 52\]

\[\begin{aligned} 3x &= 52 - 28 \\ &= 24 \end{aligned}\]

\[\begin{aligned} x &= 24 \div 3 \\ &= 8 \end{aligned}\]

Check with (2): 5 × 8 + 3 × 14 = 82.

It matches.

\[\boxed{8}\text{ euros}\]

questions.group: Q3 · Two books and a gift budget
questions.title: Two books · (c) ways to spend 150 euros
questions.prompt:
A bookshop sells two books for school: book A and book B.

Nina gets 60 euros from her parents.

She buys 3 copies of book A and 2 copies of book B, and gets 8 euros back.

Karl gets 95 euros from his parents.

He buys 5 copies of book A and 3 copies of book B, and gets 13 euros back.

(c) The head of school gives a class a gift budget of 150 euros for these two books.

The class wants at least one copy of book A and at least one copy of book B, and they must spend exactly 150 euros.

How many different ways can they do this?
questions.solution:
First find the prices from parts (a) and (b): one copy of book A costs 8 euros and one copy of book B costs 14 euros.

Now try 1 copy of book A, then 2, then 3, and so on.

Each time, check if the money left buys an exact number of copies of book B.

The ways that spend exactly 150 euros are:

\[3 \times 8 + 9 \times 14 = 150\]

\[10 \times 8 + 5 \times 14 = 150\]

\[17 \times 8 + 1 \times 14 = 150\]

\[\boxed{3}\text{ ways}\]

questions.group: Q4 · Ferry tickets and a club budget
questions.title: Ferry tickets · (a) one adult ticket
questions.prompt:
On the ferry to Gozo, every adult ticket costs the same and every child ticket costs the same.

The Vella family pays with 30 euros for 2 adult tickets and 3 child tickets, and gets 4 euros back.

The Grech family pays with 60 euros for 4 adult tickets and 5 child tickets, and gets 12 euros back.

(a) How much does one adult ticket cost?

Type the euros as a number only.
questions.solution:
Call the price of one adult ticket \(x\) euros and the price of one child ticket \(y\) euros.

First find the money spent.

The Vella family spends 30 − 4 = 26 euros.

The Grech family spends 60 − 12 = 48 euros.

Write one equation for each:

\[2x + 3y = 26 \;\;\text{(1)}\]

\[4x + 5y = 48 \;\;\text{(2)}\]

Make the number of adult tickets the same: multiply (1) by 4 and (2) by 2.

\[8x + 12y = 104\]

\[8x + 10y = 96\]

Take one away from the other, so the adult tickets disappear:

\[2y = 8\]

\[\begin{aligned} y &= 8 \div 2 \\ &= 4 \end{aligned}\]

Put \(y = 4\) back into (1):

\[2x + 3 \times 4 = 26\]

\[\begin{aligned} 2x &= 26 - 12 \\ &= 14 \end{aligned}\]

\[\begin{aligned} x &= 14 \div 2 \\ &= 7 \end{aligned}\]

Check with (2): 4 × 7 + 5 × 4 = 48.

It matches.

\[\boxed{7}\text{ euros}\]

questions.group: Q4 · Ferry tickets and a club budget
questions.title: Ferry tickets · (c) ways to spend 80 euros
questions.prompt:
